introduction: For a commercial tower on Murray Road in Central Hong Kong, double-curved satin stainless steel skins formed a lobed column enclosure whose outline changed with height. Steel ring frames and vertical members established the shape behind the segmented skin. This workshop record follows the formed pieces through a full-height dry fit, where upright lamp arrays made surface reflections easier to read and let neighboring seams be inspected together.

sections.title: A lobed column enclosure with a changing cross-section
paragraphs: The work covered the formed cladding and supporting framework for the architectural column enclosure. The design depended on two continuous lines through the height of the enclosure: the silhouette of the lobes and the narrow reveal between them. The record documents manufacturing, trial assembly and surface inspection in the workshop.

sections.title: Control the shape across formed pieces and narrow seams
paragraphs: The cladding narrows and widens in both directions. A small change in one panel edge can alter the silhouette and the reflection across the neighboring lobe. Fabrication and trial fitting therefore had to be considered together.

points.title: Compound curvature
points.text: The face was divided into formable pieces. Each piece had to follow the local curve while leaving the returns needed for the adjoining parts.

points.title: Reading waviness on satin metal
points.text: Continuous rows of inspection lamps make interruptions in the reflected line visible across a much larger area than a bench view.

points.title: Seam intersections
points.text: The vertical reveal and the transverse panel seams meet on a surface that keeps changing angle, so the fit needs to be judged across both sides of the junction.

sections.title: Formed skin segments over an internal steel framework
paragraphs: The compound face was divided into sheet segments with different profiles and return depths. The workshop photographs show the individual formed pieces and their edges before they were fitted into the standing cladding assembly.
The steel ring frame sets the cross-section at successive levels. Vertical members connect those levels, and the rear view shows the support grid behind the curved skin.

sections.title: Stand the assembly upright and read it under directional light
paragraphs: The full-height mock-ups stood on temporary workshop supports alongside vertical arrays of inspection lamps. Viewed across the face and in profile, the reflected bands showed where to look closely for waviness, changes in curvature or discontinuities across panel joints.

The workshop video walks from the satin shell to the adjacent scaffolding and exposed framework. Together with the photos, it shows how the skin and the supporting geometry were brought together at full scale.

sections.title: Satin reflections and the recessed joint between lobes
paragraphs: Close views of the standing mock-up show the backing strip recessed between the curved skins and the transverse seams approaching it from each side. The same views also show how the satin grain and reflected light read over the joint.
At the bottom of the assembly, the curved faces draw together near the floor. That part of the trial makes the relationship between the main skin and the adjacent return visible.

sections.title: What to include in a compound-curved cladding brief
paragraphs: Set out the geometry and the visual acceptance method in the same brief. A sample can establish the satin finish while a representative full-scale assembly shows how the light and seams read across the curve.

points.title: Geometry files and setting-out
points.text: Provide a CAD or STEP model with section cuts at key heights, the structural column envelope and any floor or ceiling interfaces. Mark where visible joints and removable access panels may occur.

points.title: Finish sample and mock-up lighting
points.text: Identify the desired satin grain direction, proposed seam treatment and viewing conditions. Agree what the owner will review in the sample and what needs to be seen at full scale.

points.title: Handling and installation interfaces
points.text: Provide the maximum transport envelope, unloading route, lifting access and erection clearances before setting segment lengths and dividing lines.

conclusion: This fabrication record illustrates how segmented satin stainless steel can follow a compound curve while retaining a controlled seam at full height. It is relevant to feature columns in commercial towers, public lobbies and atria. Send CAD or PDF sections with the supporting envelope, finish intent and access limits to define a useful trial-assembly scope.
